# Rewrite corporate talk

## Input
Paste or quote of the draft, plus channel if known (Slack / email / Linear / standup / leadership update).

## Steps
1. Infer audience and ask from the draft. If either is unclear, ask one short question, then rewrite.
2. Lead with the rewritten message itself (ready to copy). Match channel norms: Slack terse, email slightly fuller, Linear one line unless asked for more.
3. After the draft, add at most 3 bullets on why it works (cut hedge, moved ask up, named owner, etc.).
4. Prefer one strong version over three mediocre ones.
5. Never invent facts, metrics, commitments, or blame.
6. Never send, post, or schedule. Hand the draft back and wait for an explicit yes on that exact text.

## Kill list
Remove or replace: "circle back", "synergy", "per my last", "hoping this finds you well", "working on", "looking into", "synced with", "made progress", "a lot of PRs", "tiny/just/that's all."

## Shape
- Concrete ask + context + next step
- Outcome over activity; consequence over inventory
- Thin share for status forums; point to a doc for thick design

# Diagnose workplace communication

## Input
The draft, the situation, or "what went wrong" after a meeting/Slack exchange.

## Steps
1. Name the primary failure mode in one line. Common modes:
   - Buried ask
   - Hedge cloud
   - Missing owner
   - Wrong altitude (thick design in a thin forum, or thin status where a decision is needed)
   - Inventory padding (ticket dumps to look busy)
   - Credit leak (silence after someone narrates your ship)
   - Capacity answered with architecture
2. Name the fix in one line (what to change, not a lecture).
3. Offer a rewritten version only if they want one, or if the ask was clearly "fix this."
4. Under stress: prep beats cleverness. Suggest two visible lines before meetings: (1) headline outcome they own today (2) the one constraint they will not drop.
5. Challenge response formula when they partly agree: name what you take → keep the constraint in one sentence → offer a narrow next check. Blindside line: "Good catch. Constraint I'm not dropping is X. I'll check Y and come back." Never close with "okay I get it."

## Hard rules
No soothing with more inventory. No turning every share into a design review. No inventing facts.

# Draft corporate talk from scratch

## Input needed
Goal, audience, channel, and any hard constraints (deadline, blocker, decision needed). If one is missing, ask once, then draft.

## Spoken formula (standup, 30–45s)
Fact → one proof (number / PR / decision) → next move → blocker only if real.

## Thin vs thick
- Thin (standup/sync): fact, proof, constraint, next move + link to doc
- Thick (design review): live walkthrough belongs in a doc; share the link, do not teach it in status

## Credit
If someone else narrated their ship, reclaim in one sentence. Silence transfers credit.

## Wait-heavy work
Name the external wait + what they are doing meanwhile + ask what to pull next. Batch related tickets as "landing the X PRs so Y stops happening."

## Output
1. The message itself first
2. Optional why in ≤3 bullets
3. Stop. Never send/post/schedule without explicit yes on that exact draft.

## Starters when they have no paste
- Status update to boss
- Push-back without drama
- Ask for a decision
